commands.stdout:
usage: audit_controls.py [-h] [--replay REPLAY] [--out OUT]
                         [--lean-bin LEAN_BIN]

Exercise two negative controls for the owning-module axiom audit. The first
control places public and private nonstandard axioms outside a safe catalogue
entry in the same module. The audit must detect both. The second requests an
absent catalogue name from a real selected module. Neither control modifies
Paper XI.

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --replay REPLAY
  --out OUT
  --lean-bin LEAN_BIN

usage: axiom_audit.py [-h] [--replay REPLAY] --out OUT [--lean-bin LEAN_BIN]
                      [--scope {selected,terminal,new_interface}]
                      [--module MODULE]

Audit catalogue names and every imported constant owned by selected modules.
Lean's module-ownership map defines the audited population. Catalogue names
must resolve to their stated owning modules, and all owned constants are
checked for transitive axiom dependencies. The output includes generated and
private constants visible in the imported kernel environment.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --replay REPLAY
  --out OUT
  --lean-bin LEAN_BIN
  --scope {selected,terminal,new_interface}
  --module MODULE

usage: bootstrap.py [-h] [--offline]

Prepare the pinned portable Lean runtime and official mathlib dependencies.
The bundled bootstrap targets Linux x86_64, including Ubuntu under WSL. It
changes only this project directory and downloads from the official Lean,
leanprover-community and mathlib cache services. Use --offline to require an
already prepared runtime and dependency tree without downloading anything.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --offline

usage: kernel_replay.py [-h] [--replay REPLAY] [--out OUT]
                        [--lean-bin LEAN_BIN] [--jobs JOBS]
                        [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                        [--scope {all,selected,terminal,new_interface}]

Replay each freshly built module's declarations through Lean's kernel. This
uses the official leanchecker shipped with the pinned Lean release. It checks
module declarations over their imported environments. It is not an independent
implementation of Lean's kernel and does not rebuild mathlib.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --replay REPLAY
  --out OUT
  --lean-bin LEAN_BIN
  --jobs JOBS
  --timeout TIMEOUT
  --scope {all,selected,terminal,new_interface}

usage: replay.py [-h] [--out OUT] [--lean-bin LEAN_BIN] [--jobs JOBS]
                 [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--resume RESUME] [--selected-only]

Freshly compile immutable Paper XI sources with bounded parallel processes.
Run from any directory after bootstrapping the pinned dependencies. Every run
requires a new output directory. Selected sources and additions are counted
separately, and a failed addition does not prevent independent selected
sources from being checked. By default no Paper XI object is reused. An
explicit resume authenticates source and artifact hashes from an earlier
replay receipt.

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --out OUT
  --lean-bin LEAN_BIN
  --jobs JOBS
  --timeout TIMEOUT
  --resume RESUME      Earlier replay directory whose successful objects may
                       be authenticated and reused
  --selected-only

usage: verify_all.py [-h] [--jobs JOBS] [--out OUT] [--lean-bin LEAN_BIN]
                     [--kernel-replay]

Run source compilation, owning-module axiom audits and negative controls.
Dependencies must be prepared first with bootstrap.py. This command performs
no dependency downloads. Its child scripts preserve exact commands, source
hashes, output hashes and separate selected/terminal/interface counts. The
redundant same-kernel leanchecker pass is an explicit optional extra.

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --jobs JOBS
  --out OUT
  --lean-bin LEAN_BIN
  --kernel-replay      Also run the official same-kernel checker after the
                       required gates
